subject: radiology
title: Iodinated and Gadolinium Contrast Media and Reactions

steps.title: Iodine blocks the beam
steps.tx: **Iodinated contrast** carries iodine atoms with atomic number 53, which absorb diagnostic X-rays strongly and turn vessels and enhancing tissue white on CT. Each molecule is built on a benzene ring holding three iodine atoms. Water solubility, osmolality and ionisation of the side chains separate the generations of agents, and those chemical differences decide most of their adverse effect profiles.
steps.say: Iodinated contrast carries iodine atoms with atomic number fifty three, which absorb diagnostic X-rays strongly and turn vessels and enhancing tissue white on CT. Each molecule is built on a benzene ring holding three iodine atoms. Solubility, osmolality and side chain charge separate the generations, and those chemical differences decide most adverse effects.

steps.tx: On an axial CT angiogram, **iodinated contrast** fills the aorta and the vena cava so both lumens appear white against darker soft tissue. Iodine, atomic number 53, sits three atoms to each benzene ring and absorbs the X ray beam. Water solubility, osmolality and whether the side chains ionise decide which generation was injected, and those same chemical choices drive most adverse effects seen after the scan.

steps.title: Ionic versus non ionic agents
steps.tx: **Non ionic contrast** stays electrically neutral in solution, unlike older ionic agents that split into charged particles. Dropping the charge cut osmolality and ended most of the burning pain, nausea and haemodynamic swings of high osmolar ionic media such as diatrizoate. Low osmolar non ionic agents like iohexol and iopamidol, plus the iso osmolar dimer iodixanol, now cover almost all intravascular work.

steps.title: Contrast associated kidney injury
steps.tx: **Contrast associated acute kidney injury** means a creatinine rise within 48 to 72 hours of contrast that may or may not be caused by the agent itself. Risk concentrates in chronic kidney disease with filtration below 30, dehydration, heart failure and repeated large doses. Isotonic saline hydration before and after the study is the one protective step with consistent support, alongside withholding nephrotoxic drugs on the day.
steps.say: Contrast associated acute kidney injury means a creatinine rise within forty eight to seventy two hours that may or may not be caused by the agent itself. Risk concentrates in kidney disease with filtration below thirty, dehydration, heart failure and repeated large doses. Saline hydration before and after is the protective step with consistent support.

steps.title: Metformin and contrast
steps.tx: **Metformin** itself is not nephrotoxic; the worry is lactic acidosis if contrast triggers kidney failure while the drug accumulates. Current practice continues metformin when filtration is 30 or above and no kidney injury exists. Below 30, or with an acute kidney injury, metformin is paused at the time of contrast and restarted only after 48 hours once renal function proves stable.

steps.title: Allergy like reactions
steps.tx: **Anaphylactoid reactions** to contrast mimic allergy with urticaria, bronchospasm and hypotension but need no prior sensitisation and are not driven by IgE against the agent. Mild reactions settle with observation and antihistamines. Moderate bronchospasm needs inhaled bronchodilators and oxygen, while hypotension with airway swelling is treated exactly like anaphylaxis with intramuscular adrenaline 0.5 mg, fluids and senior help called early.

Mild reactions settle with observation and antihistamines. Airway swelling with low pressure is treated like anaphylaxis with intramuscular adrenaline, fluids and senior help called early.

steps.title: Steroid premedication
steps.tx: **Steroid premedication** is reserved for patients with a previous moderate or severe reaction to the same class of agent. A common regimen gives prednisolone 50 mg orally at 13, 7 and 1 hour before the study, with an antihistamine an hour before. Premedication lowers recurrence but never removes it, so the scan still runs with resuscitation drugs drawn up and a canula in place.

steps.title: Barium versus water soluble contrast
steps.tx: **Barium sulphate** coats mucosa superbly and is inert inside the gut lumen, but leaked barium in the peritoneum or mediastinum causes severe chemical inflammation. Suspected perforation therefore uses water soluble Gastrografin first, accepting its weaker coating. Barium in the lung irritates less than hyperosmolar Gastrografin, which pulls fluid into alveoli, so aspiration risk can reverse the choice toward barium or an iso osmolar agent.

steps.tx: Inside an intact gut, **barium sulphate** is inert and coats mucosa more clearly than water soluble contrast, the unbroken white line of a normal swallow. Leaked into the mediastinum or peritoneum it causes severe chemical inflammation, so suspected perforation is studied first with Gastrografin despite a weaker coat. In the lung the order reverses: hyperosmolar Gastrografin pulls fluid into alveoli, while barium irritates less, so aspiration risk can push the choice back to barium or an iso osmolar agent.
steps.say: Barium coats mucosa well and is safe inside an intact gut, but leaked barium inflames the mediastinum or peritoneum severely, so possible perforation is checked first with water soluble contrast. If the patient may aspirate, hyperosmolar water soluble contrast pulls fluid into alveoli, and barium or an iso osmolar agent is safer for the lung.

steps.title: Gadolinium, microbubbles and extravasation
steps.tx: **Microbubble contrast** for ultrasound uses gas filled spheres that stay inside vessels and dissolve within minutes, safe in kidney failure. Gadolinium agents instead leave vessels and distribute through extracellular fluid, with nephrogenic systemic fibrosis risk confined largely to older linear agents at filtration below 30. Contrast extravasation into soft tissue usually needs only elevation and observation, escalating only for blistering, paraesthesia or a tense compartment.
